s.t: Robert Pollard says ‘Game Of Pricks’ was already an old song when Guided By Voices made Alien Lanes; he still has the original: “slower, bouncier, and goofier.”
s.src: A Salty Salute: The Oral History Of Guided By Voices’ ’90s Indie Classic ‘Alien Lanes’ (Uproxx)
s.q: “Game Of Pricks” was an old song. I have the original version. It’s slower, bouncier, and goofier.

s.t: Grammy.com calls it arguably Guided By Voices’ signature song, and Robert Pollard seems to agree: at least once, the band played it twice in one concert.
s.src: 10 Guided By Voices Songs You Need To Hear (Grammy.com, Morgan Enos)
s.q: "Game of Pricks" is arguably GBV's signature song. (Pollard seems to think so, too: over the course of at least one concert, they've played it twice.)

s.t: Asked to pick his favourite lyrics, Robert Pollard of Guided By Voices chose a line from it, though sure there were better “out of three or four thousand songs.”
s.src: Far Out Magazine: the Guided By Voices songs Robert Pollard is proud of
s.q: ‘Game Of Pricks’ [1995]," he continued. "I'm sure there are better ones, but it's hard to think of out of three or four thousand songs.

s.t: Guided By Voices re-recorded this four-track original in a professional studio for the Tigerbomb EP later in 1995, and their best-of, Human Amusements at Hourly Rates, chose the remake.
s.q: The first two tracks are professionally recorded versions of songs from the Alien Lanes LP (the original LP versions were recorded on four-track cassette). ... Human Amusements at Hourly Rates, uses the original Alien Lanes version of "My Valuable Hunting Knife" but the re-recorded version of "Game of Pricks".

s.t: When Touché Amoré covered Guided By Voices’ song in 2021, it was outside singer Jeremy Bolm’s vocal range, so they brought in fellow GBV fan Barry Johnson of Joyce Manor.
s.src: Touché Amoré & Joyce Manor’s Barry Johnson Cover Guided By Voices’ “Game Of Pricks” (Stereogum)
s.q: and solving the problem of the song being out of Jeremy's vocal range (a great suggestion). Thinking about friends that shared love for GBV, Barry Johnson came to mind.

f.t: Their singer, Robert Pollard, pitched Wright State University’s first no-hitter on 11 May 1978, saying that had he known he was throwing one, he could never have done it.
f.src: May 11, 1978: Rocker Robert Pollard pitches first no-hitter in Wright State history (SABR Games Project)
f.q: Pollard struck out ICU's Joe Gaynor to complete the first no-hitter ... "If I had known I was in the process of throwing a no-hitter, I could never have done it,"

f.t: In 1996 Robert Pollard told The Sunday Times that Matador, not ready for another record, kept telling him to stop writing songs: “Take a vacation… watch TV.”
f.src: Stewart Lee, Guided By Voices (The Sunday Times, 7 April 1996)
f.q: "Matador keep telling me to quit writing songs for a while as they're not ready to put a new record out," concludes Pollard. "'Take a vacation,' they say, 'watch TV.' But I can't…"

f.t: Their first Matador album, Alien Lanes, came with an advance close to $100,000, yet James Greer wrote that recording it cost “about ten dollars”, leaving out the beer.
f.q: the advance for the record was close to a hundred thousand dollars, one of the more expensive deals in Matador's history. In contrast to the lucrative deal, Greer mentions that "The cost for recording Alien Lanes, if you leave out the beer, was about ten dollars."

f.t: When they first called it a day, their farewell show at the Metro in Chicago on 31 December 2004 ran four hours and 63 songs.
f.q: Guided by Voices played their final show at The Metro in Chicago on December 31, 2004.  The four-hour, 63-song marathon finale is documented on the DVD The Electrifying Conclusion.

f.t: They first won notice beyond Dayton with Propeller in 1992, pressed in just 500 copies, each with its own handmade cover.
f.q: With the release of the ultra-limited album Propeller in 1992 (of which only 500 copies were pressed, each with a unique, handmade cover), Guided by Voices for the first time gained some recognition outside of their hometown.
